owner_direction.scope: Coordinated binary32 contract work recommended in tools PR18; implementation remains in draft review.

scope: Existing six self-describing float_* comparisons; finite canonical binary32 expected operands only. No arithmetic or Result-wire extension.

observed.domain: W3C/OVAL decimal float lexical with optional exponent, INF, -INF, NaN
observed.rounding: direct decimal-to-IEEE754-binary32 roundTiesToEven; no binary64 intermediate
observed.underflow: gradual subnormal rounding and signed zero
observed.invalid: cast error; never zero, null, missing, unknown or false

expected.domain: finite JSON numbers already exactly representable as binary32, or typed references whose runtime values satisfy the same invariant
expected.source_conversion: round source decimal lexical directly to binary32, then serialize a numeric value that round-trips that exact binary32 value
expected.nonfinite: blocked, including finite source decimals that overflow binary32
expected.noncanonical: reject rather than reinterpret a binary64 approximation

comparison.signed_zero: positive and negative zero compare equal
comparison.nan_against_finite: not_equal true; all five other operations false
comparison.infinity_against_finite: negative infinity below every finite value; positive infinity above every finite value

status: Cast/comparison behavior does not replace collection, error/unknown/incomplete propagation, quantifiers, or Input provision. Existing runtime status rules remain required; this is not a scanner implementation.
serialization: Nonfinite observed bits are internal comparison states only; original observed text/provenance stays lexical. No nonfinite JSON number or new Result representation is authorized.
compatibility: Authoring schema JSON unchanged. Affected native programs require binary32 contract binding/version; old non-float program bytes remain unchanged. Historical float programs require their pinned pre-contract toolchain, never silent reinterpretation.
